questions.question: When checking tire pressure:

options.text: Looking at the tire is a good way to check it.
Squeeze the tire with your hand.
Compare how tall the tire is to another tire.

questions.explanation: Always use a tire gauge to check tire pressure before every ride. A tire that is not fully inflated may still look fine, so looking at it is not enough.

questions.question: The best source of information for your motorcycle is:

options.text: Someone who rides a different type of motorcycle.
A television show about motorcycle riding.

questions.explanation: Read the owner's manual before riding your motorcycle for the first time. This is especially important if you are riding a borrowed motorcycle. It has specific information about your bike.

questions.question: You have been drinking alcohol. If you wait one hour for each drink before riding your motorcycle:

options.text: You cannot be arrested for drinking and riding.
Your riding skills will not be affected.
You may still have effects from the alcohol in your body.
You will be fine as long as you ride slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may still have effects from the alcohol in your body.
questions.explanation: Your body can eliminate about one drink per hour. However, alcohol can still build up in your body even if you only drink one drink per hour. Your ability to ride and your judgment can still be affected.

questions.question: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects you from:
questions.explanation: A face shield protects your face from injury in a crash. It also protects you from wind, dust, dirt, rain, insects, and rocks thrown up from other vehicles.

questions.question: For the best protection, riding gloves should be made of:
questions.explanation: Gloves should be made of leather or another strong material to protect your hands.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: Mirror checks:

options.text: Should be part of your normal scanning routine.
Should be avoided because they will distract you.
Should be avoided because other drivers can see you easily.
Are only needed in bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be part of your normal scanning routine.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often to know what is behind you. Regular mirror checks should be part of how you look around while riding.

questions.question: When consuming alcohol:

options.text: Your body is not affected until you reach the legal limit for intoxication.
You feel some effects, but they are small until you reach the legal limit for intoxication.
Your ability to drive and ride is affected before you reach the legal limit for intoxication.
There is no risk if you only drink one or two drinks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your ability to drive and ride is affected before you reach the legal limit for intoxication.
questions.explanation: Alcohol affects your ability to drive and ride well before you become legally intoxicated. Even one drink can make a big difference in how well you ride.

questions.question: When riding on slippery surfaces, you should:

options.text: Avoid sudden changes in speed or direction.
Use only the front brake when stopping.
Use only the rear brake when stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid sudden changes in speed or direction.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, slow down and avoid sudden changes in speed or direction. Use both brakes when stopping.

questions.question: Unlike most food and drinks, alcohol does not need to be digested. This means that:

options.text: Within minutes of being consumed, alcohol reaches the brain and starts to affect the person.
Alcohol is never removed from the body.
It takes a long time to feel the effects of alcohol.
Once in your system, your body removes alcohol very quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Within minutes of being consumed, alcohol reaches the brain and starts to affect the person.
questions.explanation: Because alcohol does not need to be digested, it enters your bloodstream quickly and reaches your brain within minutes. Your body removes about one drink per hour.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle on a slippery surface, you should:
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, slow down. Use both brakes when braking and avoid sudden movements.

questions.question: A motorcycle operator can slow down by:
questions.explanation: Downshifting slows a motorcycle. Note that slowing down this way does not turn on the brake lights.

questions.question: You should check your tires for all of the following, except:
questions.explanation: Before each ride, check your tire air pressure, tread, and general wear.

questions.question: Most crashes happen in broad daylight. To be more visible, you should:
questions.explanation: Most crashes happen during the day. Always wear bright-colored clothing when riding, even in daylight.

questions.question: When riding, extra space around your motorcycle helps you:
questions.explanation: Extra space around your motorcycle gives you time to react if another driver makes a mistake. You need this space to maneuver safely.

questions.question: When checking tires before a ride, you should look at all of the following except:
questions.explanation: Before each ride, check your tire air pressure, tread, and general wear.

questions.question: Which of the following does not protect a motorcycle rider?
questions.explanation: Wear a DOT-approved helmet, face or eye protection, a sturdy jacket and long pants, high boots or shoes that support your ankles, and durable gloves.

questions.question: Crashes are more likely among:

options.text: Those who have taken a safety course.

questions.explanation: Beginning riders who are untrained and unfamiliar with their motorcycle are most likely to crash.

questions.question: For the best protection, make sure your helmet:
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets DOT and state standards. It should fit snugly all around with no visible defects.

questions.question: If you think stopping will take longer than usual, you should:

options.text: Increase your distance from the vehicle ahead.
Decrease your distance from the vehicle ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase your distance from the vehicle ahead.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, increase your distance from the vehicle ahead. If stopping takes longer, give yourself more following distance.

questions.question: When should you completely check your motorcycle?
questions.explanation: Motorcycles need more frequent checks than cars. Check your motorcycle completely before every ride.

questions.question: What type of helmet gives you the best protection?

options.text: One that is well-worn and broken in.

questions.explanation: Buy a helmet that meets DOT and state safety standards. It must fit snugly around your head and have no visible damage.

questions.question: What should you do to reduce your risk of a crash?

options.text: Keep your intentions hidden from other drivers.
Always stay within a foot of another vehicle.

questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, make sure other drivers can see you. Use your turn signals, brake light, and position on the road to show your intentions. Keep space around your motorcycle and watch the road ahead, behind, and beside you.

questions.question: What is required when carrying a passenger on a motorcycle?

options.text: A seat large enough for two riders.
The passenger should not wear protective clothing.
A sticker on the brake light to warn other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: A seat large enough for two riders.
questions.explanation: Only carry a passenger if your motorcycle has a seat for two riders. Your motorcycle must have footrests for the passenger. Your passenger should wear the same protective gear as the driver.

questions.question: What should you do if a driver is tailgating you?

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.
Use your horn and make rude gestures.
Speed up to create distance between you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: If you can, change lanes and let the tailgater pass. Speeding up will not help. The driver will likely tailgate you at higher speed, which is more dangerous.
